title: The Last Alibi
premise: Sable Oyelaran, the coroner of the fading mill town of Harrow Bend, has quietly proven three 'accidents' were murders, earning her a reputation as a woman who reads the dead better than the living. When the diary of missing schoolteacher Maren Voss turns up in an estate sale—with entries continuing three weeks past her disappearance—Sable realizes someone is writing as Maren, and that person wants the town to believe she's still alive. Following the forged entries, Sable uncovers a land-and-water scheme run by the county's most beloved family, who have been erasing anyone who stood in their way, including the police chief who once covered for them. The trail leads to Maren herself, alive but imprisoned by the man whose alibi she unknowingly threatened, and Sable must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the only witness who can end it. In the end, Sable trades her own credibility—her last alibi—to bring Maren home and burn the Voss conspiracy down.
about_author: Ulyana Nystrom is a former rural hospice nurse who spent a decade listening to small towns confess at bedsides before turning those confessions into fiction. She writes from a converted granary in the upper Midwest, where she keeps a ledger of every unsolved case she's ever read about.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sable Oyelaran performs the autopsy of Dale Pruitt, officially a drowning, and notes ligature marks the sheriff's report omits. Her POV establishes her quiet habit of solving what the town buries. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she talks to the dead because the living stopped listening years ago.

chapters.title: The Estate Sale
chapters.summary: At the auction of Maren Voss's belongings—declared dead in absentia—Sable buys a box of books on impulse. Tucked inside is Maren's diary. POV shifts to Maren's diary voice: bright, observant, increasingly frightened about water rights at Kestrel Reservoir. Beat: curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Three Weeks After
chapters.summary: Reading late at night, Sable finds entries dated after Maren vanished—handwriting identical, content wrong: flat, rehearsed, describing days Maren couldn't have lived. Sable compares ink and paper like evidence. Beat: cold dread; the dead don't write, so someone very much alive wants Maren remembered wrongly.

chapters.title: The Chief's Old File
chapters.summary: Sable visits retired police chief Amos Greer, who closed the Voss case, and finds him terrified, drinking, eager to change the subject. He warns her off with one word: 'Kestrel.' Beat: first open threat; Sable realizes the cover-up had a badge on it.

chapters.title: What the Water Holds
chapters.summary: Sable surveys Kestrel Reservoir, where the Aldous family's development company plans a resort, and matches Maren's final real entries to surveyors' complaints of contamination. Deputy Rhea Calloway, young and honest, quietly shares the sealed file. Beat: alliance forming; the machinery of power comes into focus.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: A handwriting analyst friend confirms the post-disappearance entries are skilled forgery—but written left-handed by a right-handed person under strain. Sable lists everyone close to Maren. Beat: methodical hope; the forger's body betrays the lie.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Aldouses
chapters.summary: Sable attends the Aldous family's charity gala under pretext, watching patriarch Everett Aldous charm the county while his son Julian watches her too closely. Julian once dated Maren. Beat: menace wrapped in hospitality; Sable understands she's being measured.

chapters.title: Amos Greer, Missing
chapters.summary: Greer doesn't show for his weekly fishing trip; his boat is found adrift, neatly moored from outside. Sable autopsies nothing yet—there's no body—and recognizes the staging echoes Dale Pruitt's case. Beat: grief and guilt; her investigation may have killed him.

chapters.title: The Third Accident
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to Sable's first quiet solve—a 'tractor rollover' two years ago—revealing the same pattern and the same beneficiary: Aldous Development. POV alternates between present Sable and memory. Beat: pattern recognition as horror; this has been happening for years.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Sable returns home to find the diary box disturbed and a page missing—the entry naming Julian. That night a car idles outside until dawn. She moves the real diary to the mortuary's cold storage, among the dead. Beat: siege mentality; nowhere safe except among corpses.

chapters.title: Rhea Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Deputy Calloway secretly runs the Pruitt DNA against old samples and gets a hit tying a county employee to the scene—then is suspended on fabricated charges within hours. Sable hides her at the funeral home. Beat: loyalty tested; the honest cop becomes a fugitive in her own town.

chapters.title: The Left-Handed Man
chapters.summary: Sable traces the forgery to Wendell Pryce, the Aldouses' estate lawyer, whose childhood injury forced left-handed writing. Confronting him gently, she cracks him: he's been ghostwriting 'Maren' letters to keep her mother compliant. Beat: pity for a collaborator; evil needs clerks.

chapters.title: Still Alive
chapters.summary: Pryce reveals what he half-knows: Maren isn't dead. Julian has kept her at the family's hunting lodge since she found contamination reports—alive because killing a teacher drew heat, imprisoned because silence was cheaper. Beat: vertigo of hope; the case flips from murder to rescue.

chapters.title: Everett's Sermon
chapters.summary: Everett Aldous publicly honors Sable at a town hall, naming her 'Harrow Bend's conscience,' a velvet warning delivered before the whole town. She smiles and accepts. Beat: corruption's politeness; power doesn't threaten loudly, it embraces you in public.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into the mortuary searching for the diary; Sable, waiting, photographs them fleeing—Julian's cousin, hired muscle. She mails copies of key pages to a state journalist as insurance. Beat: turning from prey to hunter; the dead guard her secrets well.

chapters.title: The Lodge Road
chapters.summary: Sable and Rhea scout the Aldous hunting lodge through a snowstorm, confirming a woman's silhouette at an upstairs window and a generator running out of season. They plan extraction for the night of the reservoir groundbreaking, when security thins. Beat: taut anticipation; rescue requires patience.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking
chapters.summary: At the ceremony, Sable confronts Everett privately with the diary pages, offering him one chance to release Maren quietly. He offers her money, then veiled threats against her license and reputation. Beat: the corrupt bargain refused; Sable chooses truth over safety.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Night raid: Sable and Rhea cut the lodge's power, and Sable goes in alone through the storm cellar while Rhea holds the road. She finds Maren—thin, unbroken, keeping her own secret diary on butcher paper. Julian catches them at the treeline. Beat: terror and tenderness; two diarists finally meet.

chapters.title: The Last Alibi
chapters.summary: Julian holds them at gunpoint, revealing his alibi for every crime was Maren's continued existence—her 'letters' proving she'd fled voluntarily. If she testifies, everything unravels. Sable talks him down by offering the thing he fears most made useless: she's already published. Beat: climax; words as weapons, alibi turned to confession.

chapters.title: Arrests at Dawn
chapters.summary: State police, tipped by the journalist, arrive with warrants; Everett is taken at the reservoir, Julian surrenders after firing into the air, and Pryce cooperates fully. Greer's body is found in the flooded quarry, giving Sable her fourth case—closed properly this time. Beat: catharsis; the machinery grinds, slowly, but it grinds.

chapters.title: Maren's Own Voice
chapters.summary: Maren, recovering, reads her real diary aloud at a packed community meeting, reclaiming the story that was stolen and rewritten. Sable watches the town reckon with what it applauded. Beat: identity restored; a voice returned to its owner.

chapters.title: What I Buried, What I Kept
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sable files away the Pruitt file, visits Greer's fresh grave, and accepts the interim coroner appointment with new resolve. Maren leaves her the diary's final blank pages. Beat: quiet resolution; Sable keeps the names, and now the town must hear them too.
